reply_text:
I'm adding stage faces for the marks: reading the legend's intent→stage table and how session-mode places its overlays.Now the edits: faces, the mark→stage table, and the scan step.Now a test, then the parens check, the existing tests, and loading the file.My test passes. Next I'm checking whether the two failures already fail on the committed version, using a temp copy rather than a stash.The temp copy fails more tests because of paths, so that comparison is no good. I'll read why the two tests fail instead.㊥ (colours for the C-c ; marks) In session-mode, each mark is now coloured by the loop stage of its intent: perceive is blue, believe orange, evaluate green, select amber and act pink, the same colours as the Minard figure. Gist (㊥) and unresolved (🈳) are grey, because the legend places them outside the loop. It's loaded in your Emacs; buffers already open pick it up on the next refresh (`M-x session-mode-refresh`).

🈖 (why "a few of them are already in colour") The marks that already looked coloured (🈸, 🈚, 🈯 and the rest of the 🈀 block) are drawn from the colour-emoji font. Emacs ignores the text colour on those, so each face also has a pale background in the stage colour. That way both kinds of mark show their stage. Hovering over a mark shows its intent and stage, e.g. "🈸 ask-action — ACT".

㊬ (the test) A new test checks four marks against their faces. It also checks that the session-mode table and the C-c ; menu table list the same 23 marks and intents. The two tables are kept by hand, so the test fails if one gets edited without the other. The new test passes. Two older session-mode tests fail (53 of 55 pass): both expect an analysis-request preamble in the text a REPL sends, and my change doesn't touch the send path. Committed as futon3c `97791a77`.

㊢ (families figure) Still running with zai-2; I'll bring you the link when it reports back.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(the design)
- **Panels:** eight, in the main figure's stage order.
- **Families:** up to eight per panel plus "other families" in grey.
- **Scale:** the same hits-per-day axis in every panel, so you can compare their thickness.
- **21 September marker:** labels before it come from the original 689 readings; after it, the 97 new provisional readings come into play as well.
- **Detail:** hovering shows family, day and hits. Below the panels, a table per stage gives each family's share before and after 21 September, with its top three patterns.
- **Tables in the write-up:** the same per-family tables go into `PATTERN-STAGES-2026-10-01.md`. The script generates them, so the numbers aren't typed in by hand.
- **Main figures:** left unchanged.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what will make it trustworthy) One test checks that, for every stage and day, the families add up exactly to the main figure's band. It checks against the numbers embedded in the main page, not against the new script's own totals, so a counting slip in the new script can't pass unnoticed.
